title: A novel enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay procedure in one hour by pressure incubation
protocol: Activate polystyrene surface by coating with FNAB.
Expose coated wells to UV light for 15 minutes at a wavelength of 365 nm.
Design pressure incubator from a 5-L pressure cooker.
Remove pressure regulator from the lid of the pressure cooker.
Insert one end of a 1-meter pressure tube through the vent pipe of the pressure cooker.
Connect the other end of the tube to a three-way connector.
Connect one outlay of the connector to a pressure gauge via a rubber tube and further to an argon cylinder.
Use the third outlay for releasing excess pressure and after each ELISA step.
Carry out all PELISA steps inside the pressure incubator.
Add capture molecule \(anti-human IgG) to the activated and untreated wells of a polystyrene microtiter plate.
Apply a pressure of 1.5 × 10^5 Pa using a gas cylinder inside the pressure incubator.
Maintain this pressure for 10 minutes to immobilize the capture molecule in the wells.
Release the pressure slowly after the immobilization period.
Wash the plate with washing buffer.
Block the plate by applying a pressure of 1.5 × 10^5 Pa for 10 minutes.
Release the pressure and wash the plate again with washing buffer.
Add the analyte to the wells and incubate under a pressure of 2 × 10^5 Pa for 20 minutes inside the pressure incubator.
Incubate secondary antibody-conjugate in the wells by applying a pressure of 2 × 10^5 Pa for 20 minutes inside the pressure incubator.
Add 100 µl of substrate-dye buffer at room temperature outside the pressure cooker to develop color.
Stop the color development by adding 20 µl of 5% sulfuric acid.
Record the absorbance at 490 nm.
